entities.name: PMID:25427571
observations: In vitro study of healthy-donor human adipose-derived stem cells exposed to 448-kHz capacitive-resistive electric stimulation at 50 μA/mm², 5 minutes on followed by 4 hours off.
Reported increased proliferation rate, increased S/G2/M cell-cycle fractions, and upregulation of PCNA and ERK1/2; adipogenic, chondrogenic, and osteogenic differentiation remained possible.

entities.name: Human adipose MSCs
observations: Healthy-donor human adipose-derived stem cells were the directly tested mesenchymal stem-cell source in PMID:25427571.

entities.name: 448 kHz MSC proliferation
observations: Subthermal 448-kHz stimulation increased proliferation and S/G2/M cell-cycle fractions in human adipose-derived stem cells in vitro; the abstract did not provide an absolute effect size.
No separate primary experiment in the retrieved evidence established this effect specifically in human bone-marrow-derived MSCs.
